fixes.what: The QA agent step carries no id, no step runs `jq -s -f .sdlc/bin/transcript-summary.jq` over the action's execution file, and no step calls `.sdlc/bin/agent-transcript.mjs --recover qa-report.json` — so when the QA agent finishes without writing qa-report.json, nothing records whether the Write was refused, went to a path outside the upload list, or was never made. sdlc-plan.yml and sdlc-root-cause.yml both wire all three, and agent-transcript.mjs exists for precisely this case; QA is the one artifact-emitting stage with no transcript recovery, which is why run 36983695548 produced only 'the agent did not write qa-report.json' and dispatch-fix classified it error_type=unknown. Its SHAPES map also has no 'qa-report.json' entry, so --recover would need one (keys: verdict, issue, attempt, tests, acceptance_rollup, next_action).
fixes.fix: Give the QA agent step an id (e.g. `id: qa_agent`), add a step after it — `if: always()`, env EXEC from `steps.qa_agent.outputs.execution_file` — running `jq -s -f .sdlc/bin/transcript-summary.jq "$EXEC" > qa-transcript.json || true`, add qa-transcript.json to the qa-evidence upload path list, and add a `--recover qa-report.json` invocation of agent-transcript.mjs in the judge job before the validate step; extend SHAPES in .sdlc/bin/agent-transcript.mjs with the qa-report.json key list. That makes a recovered report subject to the same validator and gates as a written one, and prints the tool-call metadata that lets triage tell a refused Write from a missing one.
fixes.diagnosis: The QA agent ran to completion and did its job; it just never wrote the one file the workflow gates on. The action returned subtype=success, is_error=false after 323 turns / 51 minutes / $20.19, so the step is green, and the agent left 24 evidence files in qa-evidence/ (a 636-line three-file Playwright suite, 19 screenshots, a HAR, a trace, plus an out-of-band better-sqlite3 check against the Electron registration). check-evidence.mjs then said the report could not be read and the judge's validate rejected it by name — but that is the last step of a long chain, not the break. The break is that nothing in the qa workflow looks at what the agent actually did. The action writes the full transcript to _temp/claude-execution-output.json and the log prints only a metadata line about it; sdlc-qa.yml gives the agent step no id, never runs jq -s -f .sdlc/bin/transcript-summary.jq over that file, and never calls agent-transcript.mjs --recover. sdlc-plan.yml and sdlc-root-cause.yml both do all three, and agent-transcript.mjs was written for exactly this failure (growth-os #20: an agent that reported success and wrote neither expected file). QA is the one agent-emitting stage with no transcript recovery, so this failure mode is structurally invisible here: whether the Write was refused, was aimed at a path outside the upload list, or was simply never made is not answerable from anything this run kept. A prior instance is recorded in the workflow's own comment at sdlc-qa.yml:620-622 ('validate then said the agent did not write qa-report.json and triage answered with another browser session'), and the fix applied then tightened the artifact download — which was a different failure and is why this one recurred undiagnosed. I did not rule out a bad agent run, and I am not claiming one: the evidence shows the suite was built and run and the fix's guard verified working on both platforms, so the QA work is sound. What is missing is not the testing, it is the report and any way to see why it was not written. That is a defect in the pipeline's plumbing, so it escalates rather than re-running: a rerun would burn another ~$20 and ~50 minutes to reach the same dead end, and the next agent would have exactly as much visibility as this one did.
fixes.evidence: test job, 'Test it, adversarially': {"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"duration_ms":3098783,"num_turns":323,"total_cost_usd":20.19} — success, then 'Did the evidence survive?' logs 'the QA report cannot be read (ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'qa-report.json')', and judge logs 'sdlc: the agent did not write qa-report.json'. Meanwhile upload-artifact reports 'there will be 24 files uploaded' and the qa-evidence artifact (ID 11218775655, 16569296 bytes) downloads intact in judge — so the evidence survived and only the report is missing. The workflow gap: .github/workflows/sdlc-qa.yml has no `id:` on the agent step (so no `steps.<id>.outputs.execution_file`, cf. sdlc-plan.yml:360 and sdlc-root-cause.yml:333), no `jq -s -f .sdlc/bin/transcript-summary.jq` step, and no `agent-transcript.mjs` call (grep for 'transcript' in sdlc-qa.yml returns nothing), while agent-transcript.mjs's own header names this exact failure ('ran 22 turns, reported success, and wrote neither work-order.json nor stop.json ... triage could not tell a Write that was refused from one never made'). Survived work, if a person wants it: PR #11 (OPEN, MERGEABLE, head b635e0f), artifact qa-evidence with qa-evidence/spec/{regexp,regexp-edge}.spec.ts + fixtures.ts, electron-variant-check.txt showing the guard returning 0 for `\`, `#\`, `#[`, `(` and 1 for `#mortgage` on better-sqlite3, and served-tree-probe.txt confirming the preview serves _pr/ at b635e0f with the guard present. Ruled out: transient/outage/limit (a 51-minute agent run completed with is_error=false, no 429/529/timeout, and prior_signatures is empty); a defect in the app's own code (served-tree-probe and electron-variant-check both show the PR's guard installed and semantically correct); a bad work order (work-order.json is intact on the ledger at version 1 and QA's suite maps to its six acceptance criteria).
